system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran confrontation and urgent diplomacy amid regional spillover
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapidly escalating US–Iran confrontation — fought directly and via regional proxies — dominates the news as the Trump administration conducts intense negotiations while Iran exerts military and political pressure. As an open system this narrative comprises interacting state and non‑state actors (US, Iran, Israel, Lebanon, Gulf states, militias), flows of military action, diplomatic signaling, sanctions/financial measures and humanitarian effects, and feedback loops where strikes, domestic politics, and mediation attempts change incentives and propagate instability across borders. The dynamic produces knock‑on effects across adjacent theatres (Gaza, Lebanon) and influences global diplomacy and public opinion.
system_description.scope: Direct conflict and diplomacy between the US and Iran, regional military escalations (Israel–Lebanon, Gaza), mediation efforts by third states (Qatar, Rome talks), related sanctions/financial moves, and immediate humanitarian and political consequences within affected states.
system_description.super_system: Regional and global security order (international diplomacy, conflict management, and stability of the Middle East within global geopolitics)
adjacent_subsystems: Gulf states diplomacy and energy/geopolitical calculations
US domestic politics and electoral considerations

variables.name: Military escalation level
variables.description: The aggregate intensity of direct military operations and kinetic engagements among state-level armed forces in the region.

variables.name: Proxy attack rate
variables.description: The frequency at which non‑state or proxy forces carry out offensive actions attributable to major actors.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The volume and energetic level of formal and informal diplomatic contacts, negotiations, and signaling between rival parties and third parties.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure strength
variables.description: The aggregate severity and reach of economic and financial restrictive measures applied to coerce or punish actors.

variables.name: Financial channel disruption
variables.description: The degree to which banking, payment, and trade finance channels are constrained, interrupted, or subject to risk premia across the system.

variables.name: Humanitarian casualty flow
variables.description: The rate of civilian deaths and injuries resulting from hostilities and related secondary effects (e.g., collapse of services).

variables.name: Population displacement flow
variables.description: The rate and volume of internal displacement and cross‑border refugee movements driven by conflict and insecurity.

variables.name: Public support for conflict
variables.description: The prevailing level of popular approval or tolerance for continued military confrontation among affected domestic populations.

variables.name: Political constraint on leaders
variables.description: The strength of domestic political pressures, electoral considerations, and elite bargaining that limit or compel leadership choices on conflict.

variables.name: Third‑party mediation capacity
variables.description: The availability and effectiveness of neutral external actors and institutional channels able to mediate, shuttle‑diplomacy, or broker arrangements.

variables.name: Regional alliance cohesion
variables.description: The degree of alignment, trust, and coordinated action among neighboring actors and security partners in the theatre.

variables.name: Arms transfer flow
variables.description: The rate and volume of weapons, munitions, and military materiel shipments moving into and within the conflict system.

variables.name: Information‑warfare intensity
variables.description: The scale and aggressiveness of propaganda, disinformation, and strategic communications campaigns aimed at shaping perceptions and legitimacy.

variables.name: Command‑and‑control cohesion
variables.description: The internal coherence, discipline, and functional integrity of military and paramilitary command structures.

variables.name: Cross‑border incident frequency
variables.description: The occurrence rate of discrete transboundary incidents (strikes, raids, airspace violations) that transmit instability across borders.

catalysts.title: US–Iran negotiations potentially produce agreement
catalysts.description: Intensive US–Iran talks could yield a near‑term understanding or limited deal, altering coercive measures and lowering active hostilities if implemented. Talks face denial and domestic pushback.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'US and Iran having 'very good discussions','Trump says deal is near','Trump says US held all-day negotiation' indicate a likely active negotiation track.

catalysts.title: Qatar mediation advances
catalysts.description: Qatari mediators report progress in shuttle diplomacy that could bolster third‑party channels and enable temporary de‑escalation steps between US, Iran and regional actors.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Qatar says mediators make progress in efforts to end US-Iran war' drives expectation of stronger mediation channels.

catalysts.title: Escalation along Lebanon–Israel front
catalysts.description: Following soldier deaths and evacuation warnings, strikes in south Lebanon risk a spike in cross‑border incidents, civilian harm and local displacement in the coming days.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Israel strikes southern Lebanon after evacuation warning' and 'Israeli military issues evacuation warning' indicate immediate cross‑border risk.

catalysts.title: Iran issues warnings to Gulf states
catalysts.description: Public Iranian threats to Gulf states could prompt retaliation, heighten proxy mobilization, and reduce regional cooperation and diplomatic space if followed by reprisals.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EXCLUSIVE: Iran warns Gulf states: tell Trump to desist or we hit you hard' signals increased regional targeting risk.

catalysts.title: Further targeted U.S. sanctions relief
catalysts.description: Following the Fly Baghdad delisting, the US may pursue additional limited sanctions relaxations to facilitate talks, reducing economic pressure on Iran‑linked channels.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US lifts sanctions on Fly Baghdad' implies a precedent for targeted relief tied to diplomatic progress.

catalysts.title: Rome talks continue on de‑escalation
catalysts.description: Ongoing talks in Rome among regional actors aim to limit spillover and could produce confidence‑building steps that lower kinetic tempo if they hold.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Israel strikes ... talks continue in Rome' shows an active multilateral de‑escalation track.

catalysts.title: Political fallout from Israeli sacking of general
catalysts.description: The defence minister's high‑profile dismissal could disrupt military command cohesion and shape domestic constraints on strategic decisions during the campaign.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Israel’s defence minister triggers row after sacking general on TV' implies near‑term command and political effects.

catalysts.title: Rising US public concern over Middle East chaos
catalysts.description: Polls showing Americans bracing for more chaos raise political pressure on US leaders to limit escalation and seek diplomatic exits.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'As Iran war drags on, Americans are bracing for more chaos in Middle East, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds' signals growing domestic pressure.
